hero.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as grocery shoppers seek relief from rising food costs
hero.body:
A new Aldi store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable grocery options to Martin County residents facing rising food costs. The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8 percent this year, with fruits and vegetables seeing an increase of less than 1 percent.

Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited an affordable option like Aldi is now open close to their home. "We're thrilled to have it here," Cheryl said. "Now we have something with reasonable prices that's close by." She said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. "We're the type of people who never used to look at prices," Cheryl said. "I will go with what's on sale instead of just with what we want, and we never used to do that."

Egg prices are dropping and beef prices fell 1.3 percent from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1 percent from April to May and chicken prices rose 1.3 percent over the same period. The price increases continue to put strain on family budgets as shoppers look for ways to reduce their grocery bills.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated; they're not gonna go down. It's just I'd be willing to bet on that," they said. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. "Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial, because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase and stuff."

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher shot and killed; family member arrested
cards.teaser: Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce community is mourning the loss of Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children.

His family released a statement about his death, saying they are sad to report the loss of their dad to a senseless act of violence. The family asked people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online discussing any other details as this is still an active investigation and a deeply painful circumstance that impacts so many people. Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as a pillar of the community and a father figure to students who didn't grow up with a dad. Coleman, now 37 years old, said Barnes made an impact on them life-long and they kept communication well before social media even came around.

cards.headline: Two bodies found near Sebastian remain under investigation, appear unconnected but suspicious, sheriff says
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Thursday that two bodies found near Sebastian this week appear unconnected but remain under investigation. James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident, was found Monday on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. On Wednesday shortly after 4 p.m., a second body, heavily decomposed, was located in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian, across the street from Monday's location.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said at a Thursday morning news conference that Thompson had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian and was last seen Sunday walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1 around 1:30 p.m. Thompson had a history of fentanyl use and mental health issues and had made a purchase of methamphetamine on July 3, entering a manic state, according to Flowers. The sheriff said Thompson had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County many times. The second body was a 65-year-old man with a temporary address with his brother in Sebastian who was out of jail on pretrial release after being arrested by Plantation police on a charge of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon in Broward County. The man had a serious history of seizures and walked away from a hospital Sunday morning against medical advice. The man's brother took him to the hospital Sunday, and he was still wearing hospital socks when he left. His brother last saw him walking north at 7:30 a.m. Sunday.

Flowers said autopsies on both bodies revealed no stab wounds or evidence of violence. Thompson had only a minor contusion on his eyebrow. The sheriff said the investigation remains active until toxicology results determine the cause of death. Flowers said both cases are still considered suspicious, noting that any death that is not a natural death is suspicious. He warned that bad fentanyl or methamphetamine could be on the streets and urged drug users to seek treatment. Plantation police had obtained a warrant for the 65-year-old man for absconding on his pretrial release by being in Indian River County.

Jim Sullivan, a resident who lives in the area, said the community is very nice and has low crime. Sullivan said the two bodies were found about a football field's length apart and within a straight line of sight from his bedroom window. He said it was comforting to know the deaths appear unrelated but still disconcerting. Anyone with information in either case is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranked 67th most stressed city in United States
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie was tabbed as the 42nd most financially stressed city in America, according to a WalletHub study released this month that compared 182 cities across 39 metrics.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie was ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the United States, according to a WalletHub study released this month. The report cited that the city is the 42nd most financially stressed in America. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics, which included average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates.

Jacksonville is the most stressed city in Florida, topping out at No. 37 in the United States. Florida performed fairly well compared to other states, with no cities in the top 35. In South Florida, Miami was on the list at No. 50, with affordable housing being fourth worst in the country, and Fort Lauderdale at No. 83. WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors. Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities in the country. Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, topped the list of least stressed, followed by South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota.

cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets committed five errors and gave up 17 hits in a 15-3 loss to the Jupiter Hammerheads on Camp Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday afternoon.

Jupiter scored in each of its final seven innings at the plate, steadily pulling away after the Mets grabbed an early lead.

Antonio Jimenez put St. Lucie ahead 2-1 with a two-run homer in the third inning, his second home run in the last three games and his fifth of the season with the Mets. The lead did not last. Jupiter answered with four runs in the bottom of the third to go up 5-2, keyed by a two-run single from Max Williams and an RBI double from Nixon Chirinos.

Jackson Hauge trimmed the deficit to 5-3 with a two-out RBI single in the fourth, but that was the last Mets hit until Elian Peña singled with one out in the eighth. In between, Jupiter reliever Elier Morillo retired all 10 batters he faced, striking out seven.

The Hammerheads kept adding on, scoring two in the fourth, two in the fifth and four in the sixth, the last punctuated by a three-run homer from Chirinos off Caden Wooster.

All nine Jupiter starters reached base and eight collected hits. Leadoff man Luis Cova went 4 for 5, a triple shy of the cycle, while Williams finished 2 for 5 with a homer, three RBI and three runs. For St. Lucie, Peña, Branny De Oleo and Francisco Toledo each went 2 for 4.

Mets starter Christian Rodriguez took the loss, charged with five runs on eight hits over three innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out five.

The Mets (4-12, 37-45) and Hammerheads (7-11, 44-40) continue their series Friday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida's updated Live Local Act takes effect, expanding affordable housing opportunities
cards.teaser: Florida's updated Live Local Act took effect today, expanding affordable housing opportunities across the state.
cards.body:
The updated Live Local Act took effect Thursday, expanding affordable housing opportunities throughout Florida. The law is generating debate at the local level about its implementation and impact on communities statewide.

The legislation represents Florida's effort to address housing affordability challenges across the state. Local governments and housing advocates are evaluating how the changes will affect development and access to affordable housing in their areas.

hero.headline: Park Vista Cobras football team aims for state playoffs after strong finish to 2025 season
hero.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The team struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games.

"Felt good throughout the second half of that season," senior Harris Bender said. "We're just working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, like you said, and we have all the pieces in place now, it's just about executing." The Cobras are focused on maintaining that second-half performance throughout the entire 2026 campaign as they pursue their championship aspirations.

The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017. "We got to take it one game at a time," Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs." The coach's measured approach emphasizes the importance of focusing on each opponent rather than looking too far ahead. Senior Erik Lee echoed that mindset, saying, "Coming in, I feel like we got the guys that we need to get it done. But also, we got to put the work in to get there as well."

Senior Justice Jones expressed confidence about reaching the program's goals. "It's going to feel amazing, because I already know it's gonna happen, definitely," Jones said. The returning players believe the pieces are in place for a successful season if they can execute their game plan and maintain their work ethic. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August debut
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League announced the nicknames and logos of its four teams, each inspired by pioneering women, as the league prepares for its inaugural season starting August 1.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The league also includes the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters. The WPBL's debut season begins on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs.

The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as "Firebelle," who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. Their logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the "Queen of the Diamond." The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist. Their logo is an osprey clasping a baseball bat in its talons. "This is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball," Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March, "and now for us to actually be with each other, there's so much freedom and peace within it."

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Egypt in World Cup round of 16
cards.teaser: Argentina scored three goals in the final 11 minutes of regulation time to rally from a 2-0 deficit and defeat Egypt 3-2, with Lionel Messi scoring his eighth goal of the tournament.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to an improbable 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday despite trailing by two with only 11 minutes of regulation time to play. The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete one of the great World Cup comebacks. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute.

Argentina had trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. Messi missed a chance in the first half when his penalty kick was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir. He later hit the post when the score was 1-0. Despite being the all-time leading scorer at World Cups, Messi has now missed four of eight penalty kicks at the tournament. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said he was emotional about the group of players.

cards.headline: US-Belgium World Cup match draws record 30 million viewers, becomes most-watched soccer telecast in American history
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match drew more than 30 million viewers on Fox Sports, peaking at 36 million early in the second half despite the US losing 4-1.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported. According to Fox, the match drew more than 30 million viewers. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: Justin Bieber, Madonna, and BTS to headline World Cup final halftime show at New York on July 19
cards.teaser: FIFA announced Wednesday that Justin Bieber will join Madonna, Shakira, and BTS for an 11-minute halftime performance during the World Cup final, supporting a $100 million education fund.
cards.body:
Justin Bieber will bring his swag to the World Cup's star-studded, Super Bowl-style halftime show, joining fellow headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS, FIFA announced Wednesday. Afrobeats star Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus, a choir of elementary school students based in Staten Island, New York, will also perform, the last joined by Coldplay. The 11-minute halftime performance, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin, will take place during the final outside New York on July 19. The show will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which is raising $100 million to help children access education and soccer. This year's World Cup halftime performance will also feature some characters from "Sesame Street," as well as Muppets like Kermit and Miss Piggy.

The addition of Burna Boy is particularly noteworthy because he's one-half of this year's official song for the World Cup, "Dai Dai," led by Shakira. The song is a mesh of their musical landscapes, combining Afrobeats and Latin rhythms into a multilingual pop track. In one verse, they name famous soccer players and countries competing in this year's World Cup. "The FIFA World Cup brings the world together in a way nothing else can," Bieber said in a statement. Burna Boy said representing Africa on the first-ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show is a privilege and a responsibility that he doesn't take lightly.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff in dramatic Wimbledon semifinal tiebreaker to reach final
cards.teaser: Ninth-ranked Karolina Muchova ended seventh-ranked Coco Gauff's Wimbledon run Thursday with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory, becoming the fourth Czech woman to reach the final in six years.
cards.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, champion in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The festival is scheduled for November 2026 in Vero Beach. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. is organizing the event.

The Treasure Coast Seafood Festival has been an annual event in Vero Beach for 17 years. The festival will mark its 18th year when it returns this fall.

Additional details about the November festival dates, location, and vendors were not included in the announcement from Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

cards.headline: Neighbors push back on proposed 85-acre Indrio Town Center development
cards.teaser: A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but neighbors say it will transform the area's rural character.
cards.body:
A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but neighbors say it will transform the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August. The proposed development includes 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres.

Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades. Lewis said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. She has dogs and horses that currently have 10 acres to run around. County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development. Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, representing property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will include open green space and an over 26-acre park.

hero.headline: Two bodies found near Sebastian remain under investigation, appear unconnected but suspicious, sheriff says
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Thursday that two bodies found near Sebastian this week appear unconnected but remain under investigation. James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident, was found Monday on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. On Wednesday shortly after 4 p.m., a second body, heavily decomposed, was located in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian, across the street from Monday's location.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said at a Thursday morning news conference that Thompson had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian and was last seen Sunday walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1 around 1:30 p.m. Thompson had a history of fentanyl use and mental health issues and had made a purchase of methamphetamine on July 3, entering a manic state, according to Flowers. The sheriff said Thompson had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County many times. The second body was a 65-year-old man with a temporary address with his brother in Sebastian who was out of jail on pretrial release after being arrested by Plantation police on a charge of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon in Broward County. The man had a serious history of seizures and walked away from a hospital Sunday morning against medical advice. The man's brother took him to the hospital Sunday, and he was still wearing hospital socks when he left. His brother last saw him walking north at 7:30 a.m. Sunday.

Flowers said autopsies on both bodies revealed no stab wounds or evidence of violence. Thompson had only a minor contusion on his eyebrow. The sheriff said the investigation remains active until toxicology results determine the cause of death. Flowers said both cases are still considered suspicious, noting that any death that is not a natural death is suspicious. He warned that bad fentanyl or methamphetamine could be on the streets and urged drug users to seek treatment. Plantation police had obtained a warrant for the 65-year-old man for absconding on his pretrial release by being in Indian River County.

Jim Sullivan, a resident who lives in the area, said the community is very nice and has low crime. Sullivan said the two bodies were found about a football field's length apart and within a straight line of sight from his bedroom window. He said it was comforting to know the deaths appear unrelated but still disconcerting. Anyone with information in either case is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.
